intro: Foundations of International Law. Unit four: customary international law — how a rule comes into being without anybody legislating.

slides.5: What evidences opinio iuris. Conclusion 10, paragraph 2 lists public statements made on behalf of states, official publications, government legal opinions, diplomatic correspondence, decisions of national courts, treaty provisions, and conduct in connection with resolutions of international organizations. Compare that list with the list of what evidences state practice, and you will see that the same act — a diplomatic note, a national judgment — can serve as evidence of both elements. That is why an answer must say which element it is using an act for, and why, rather than simply listing acts.
slides.6: The Lotus case, the facts. The Lotus was a French mail steamer. In 1926 it collided on the high seas with a Turkish vessel; when the Lotus reached Istanbul, a French naval officer was taken into custody and criminally charged by Turkey. France protested, relying on the flag-state principle: only the flag state may prosecute for acts on board. The question put to the Permanent Court was whether international law permitted Turkey to exercise jurisdiction.
slides.11: The North Sea Continental Shelf cases. Picture the North Sea with maritime boundaries drawn between the United Kingdom, Norway, Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium and France. The dispute was about how to delimit the shelf between Germany on one side and Denmark and the Netherlands on the other. Because the German coast is concave, the equidistance method would have squeezed Germany's shelf into a narrow wedge. Germany was not party to the 1958 Convention containing the equidistance rule, so the question became whether that rule had become customary.
slides.17: How much time custom needs. None, in principle. The North Sea cases said the period may be short, provided the practice is extensive and virtually uniform. Two examples show how fast it can go. The Truman Proclamation of 1945, after which coastal states' claims to the continental shelf spread within a few years. And the Sputnik flights of 1957 over foreign territory, met without protest, from which the freedom of outer space followed. Duration is evidence of settled practice, not a requirement in itself.
slides.20: Is codification a good thing? Five advantages against three disadvantages. In favour: systematization, precision, progressive development, the articulation of community interests, and legitimization. Against: it can block further legal development by freezing the law; the text is a compromise and tends towards the lowest common denominator; and a failed codification creates legal insecurity, because afterwards nobody is sure what the customary position was. That last point is the one most often missed.
